primary-500.note: Default scheme (:root and [data-color-scheme="blue"]). Canonical in the frontmatter.

primary-500-emerald.note: Alternate runtime scheme [data-color-scheme="emerald"]. Full ramp, not a tint of blue.

primary-500-violet.note: Alternate runtime scheme [data-color-scheme="violet"]. Full ramp, not a tint of blue.

surface-body.note: Page body. Per scheme: blue #f8fafc/#0f172a, emerald #f0fdf4/#071a12, violet #faf5ff/#120b20 (light/dark).

surface-card.note: Raised reading surface. Light is #ffffff in all three schemes; dark differs: blue #1e293b, emerald #0f2e24, violet #1e1b4b.

surface-panel-alt.note: Toolbars and filter bars. blue #f1f5f9/#1e293b, emerald #ecfdf5/#14332a, violet #f5f3ff/#2d1f4e.

surface-chrome.note: Sidebar, header, footer, dropdown. Dark in both modes. blue #1e293b/#020617, emerald #14332a/#020c09, violet #2d1f4e/#0f0620.

border-default.note: Defines every surface edge. Tinted per scheme: blue #e2e8f0/#334155, emerald #bbf7d0/#14532d, violet #e9d5ff/#6b21a8.

text-muted.note: Secondary copy and metadata. Tinted per scheme: blue #64748b/#94a3b8, emerald #047857/#6ee7b7, violet #6d28d9/#c4b5fd.

surface-release-row.note: Listing row surface, tuned separately from cards because it repeats hundreds of times. Scheme-independent (:root only).

display.purpose: Page titles at sm and above. Rare.

headline.purpose: The x-page-header title, with an accent icon.

body.purpose: The 14px baseline. The app's dominant size by a wide margin.

label.purpose: Chips, badges, metadata, table headers, small controls.

modes.name: dark
modes.note: Class-based: @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)). Independent of colorScheme; 3 schemes x 2 modes = 6 realisations.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Gentle lift on .card, on top of its 1px border. Borders lead; shadow is secondary.

shadows.name: dropdown
shadows.purpose: Menus and popovers floating above the page.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, the deepest level in the stack.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Body background-colour transition on theme change, 200ms.

motionGaps.name: prefers-reduced-motion
motionGaps.note: Zero occurrences across resources/ as of 2026-09-20, while csp-safe.css ships transitions and fadeIn/pulse keyframes. Recorded as an observed gap, not a rule.

extensions.breakpointsNote: Tailwind v4 defaults. The project overrides none of them; there is no tailwind.config file.

outOfScope.name: forum
outOfScope.note: Separate preset, own Vite entrypoint and x-forum::button family.

outOfScope.name: pulse
outOfScope.note: Laravel Pulse uses Livewire and its own styling.

outOfScope.name: admin control sizes
outOfScope.note: Admin keeps its existing component sizes; the .public-ui scale does not apply there.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action. Bordered even though filled, so the shape holds on any surface.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem; height:42px; padding:0.5rem 1rem; border-radius:0.5rem; border:1px solid transparent; font-family:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.875rem; font-weight:600; line-height:1.5; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px #fff,0 0 0 4px var(--color-primary-500,#3b82f6); } .ds-btn-primary { background:var(--color-primary-600,#2563eb); border-color:var(--color-primary-600,#2563eb); color:#fff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:var(--color-primary-700,#1d4ed8); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action beside a primary one.

components.name: Input Control
components.description: The shared public control scale: 42px tall, 8px radius, 14px text. Applies where the control is inside .public-ui; outside it, x-input's own utility baseline renders instead.
components.css: .ds-control { height:42px; padding:0 14px; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid var(--border-default,#e2e8f0); background:var(--surface-card,#fff); color:#374151; font-family:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:14px; line-height:1.5; } .ds-control:focus { outline:none; border-color:var(--color-primary-500,#3b82f6); box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--color-primary-500,#3b82f6); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The raised reading surface. Border defines it; shadow lifts it slightly. .card owns no padding in the source — the 1.5rem here exists only so the snippet renders.
components.html:
Release

Border leads, shadow is secondary.
components.css: .ds-card { background:var(--surface-card,#fff); border:1px solid var(--border-default,#e2e8f0); border-radius:0.75rem; box-shadow:0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1),0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); padding:1.5rem; font-family:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { margin:0 0 0.5rem; font-size:1.125rem; font-weight:600; color:#111827; } .ds-card-body { margin:0; font-size:0.875rem; color:var(--text-muted,#64748b); }

components.name: Chip
components.description: A readout, not decoration. Reports completion, preview availability, origin or category.
components.css: .ds-chip { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:0.25rem; background:var(--surface-panel-alt,#f1f5f9); color:#374151; border-radius:0.5rem; padding:0.125rem 0.5rem; font-family:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.75rem; font-weight:500; line-height:1.5; } .ds-chip-success { background:#dcfce7; color:#166534; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: The pill form. Five tones, three sizes, always fully rounded.
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; background:var(--color-primary-100,#dbeafe); color:var(--color-primary-800,#1e40af); border-radius:9999px; padding:0.125rem 0.625rem; font-family:Figtree,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.75rem; font-weight:500; }

narrative.maintainerStatement: Visually appealing, easy to navigate, and easy to absorb the information being shown.
narrative.overview: NNTmux is a catalogue you retrieve from, lit well enough that you can read it. The collection is enormous and mostly machine-generated, so the interface's job is to make a wall of releases legible: what this thing is, whether it is complete, whether it is worth taking. Chips are the instrumentation and they are read at a glance rather than studied. The system serves two audiences on one chassis: the public side browses, searches and evaluates; the admin side operates the indexer that fills it. Its defining structural fact is that the palette is not fixed. Three accent schemes are selectable at runtime, each with its own complete eleven-step ramp, each crossing an independent light/dark axis.
keyCharacteristics: Runtime-swappable accent across three schemes; class-based dark mode on top
A 14px body baseline: the app reads dense even where controls are comfortable
One text family, Figtree, carrying the whole hierarchy by weight and size
Borders define surfaces; shadow is a gentle secondary lift
Status colour is semantic and literal; the accent belongs to actions and navigation

rules.name: The Borrowed Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is on loan from the user. Any component that bakes in a blue, emerald or violet value has broken two of the three schemes. Use primary-* utilities; if a value must be literal, it is a status colour and should say so.

rules.name: The Chip Is a Readout Rule
rules.body: Chips report state; they are not decoration and not navigation by another name. A chip that does not tell the reader something they would otherwise have to open the release to learn does not belong on the row.

dos: Use primary-* for accent, links, focus rings and selected states.
Give every colour utility a dark: counterpart unless a token or ancestor handles it.
Reuse x-button, the input/select/textarea/label set, and the semantic surface classes.
Put styles in csp-safe.css or utilities; the Alpine CSP build rejects inline style attributes.
Keep status colour literal and semantic.
donts: Don't hardcode an accent hex. Three schemes break at once.
Don't introduce a second text family or a second icon library.
Don't assume slate neutrals. Emerald and violet tint their borders and muted text.
Don't reach for shadow where a border would do.
Don't extend font-extrabold, and don't add border weights beyond 1px.

enforcement.runsIn: frontend verification lane; scripts/agent-verify gates it behind `if frontend:`, and it is a required CI command in .github/ci-policy.json
enforcement.principle: Every check inspects class names, not values. The rules constrain how a value is reached, never what the value is. A redesign that replaces palette, type scale, spacing and component language passes all of them untouched, provided it routes through the token layer. See the script's own comment at line 26.

indirectionRules.rule: no literal blue-* accent utility in views; use primary-*
forum primary-* utilities need an explicit dark: treatment
no hardcoded bg-white / bg-gray-N in public views; use semantic surfaces or tokens
no indigo-*/purple-* accent utilities in public views; use primary-*
no blue-* accent utility assigned from JavaScript; use primary-*

hygieneRules.rule: no Bootstrap btn shim; use x-button / x-button-link
Font Awesome is the only icon library (no feather)
hygieneRules.open: whether a replacement design keeps this constraint is deliberately unsettled

hygieneRules.rule: no inline style attributes; CSP constraint, not a preference
fixed Vue action panels need v-cloak

hygieneRules.open: tied to the icon-library question above

enforcement.descriptiveOnly: narrative.dos and narrative.donts below, and everything else in DESIGN.md, are description rather than law. No check inspects them and a redesign may overturn any of them.
